Sumaiya Essa

Educational Psychology & Guidance · Special Education · Inclusive Learning

I believe every learner thinks and grows differently, and that belief shapes everything I do.
My work moves between classrooms, research fields, and program teams-
from teaching children with special needs, to running household surveys in rural communities.
I'm currently pursuing my Master's in Educational Psychology & Guidance at IER, University of Dhaka.
What draws me to this field is the space between theory and practice;
taking what research tells us about how people learn, and turning it into something usable.
I care about inclusion not as a policy word, but as a daily classroom practice.
I'm equally at home facilitating a focus group discussion and preparing an IEP.
Every role I've taken from teaching, research, to coordination has sharpened the same instinct:
notice the learner in front of you, not just the curriculum.
This portfolio is a record of that instinct in motion.

About

I'm currently pursuing a Master of Education in Educational Psychology & Guidance at IER, University of Dhaka, following a Bachelor of Education in Special Education from the same institute. Alongside my studies, I teach at a special needs school, support university-based research on education policy, and have spent the last two years moving through classrooms, research fields, and program offices — from inclusive classrooms in Dhaka to household surveys on water security and climate resilience.

What ties this together is a consistent interest in how people learn differently, and how systems like schools, programs, policies can be built to notice that. I'm drawn to the practical side of educational psychology: understanding how individual learners think and grow, and turning that understanding into classrooms, programs, and research that actually serve them.

Outside of academic and professional work, I stay involved with cultural and volunteer initiatives — from coordinating events with the IER Language and Cultural Club to supporting local education forums.
